interactions.summary: Statius explains that the soul becomes fully free to climb only when purity is proven, even though the desire to keep doing penance can delay ascent for centuries.
Jiang turns Statius's lines into a classroom interrogation about why purgatorial souls suffer, rejecting weak paraphrases and pressing students toward a free-will account of penance.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led class exchange with multiple student attempts.

claims.claim: Statius says the will becomes the proof of purity, and that souls can already want to ascend while still also wanting to keep doing penance under divine justice.
The same speaker says he has lain in this suffering for more than five hundred years and only now feels the free will that lets him cross to a better threshold.
Jiang frames the key interpretive problem as why souls in purgatory undergo punishment at all if they already have the will to climb.
One student proposes that purgatory tests whether the soul's mindset has really changed from hell's.
Another student offers that sin still weighs the soul down and therefore has to be cleansed before further ascent is possible.

signature_moments.moment: Purity is measured by a will that becomes fully free enough to change dwelling place.
signature_moments.source_phrase: The will alone is proof of purity
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's central definition of purgatorial freedom.

signature_moments.moment: The soul's ascent is delayed not merely by punishment from outside but by an inward longing to continue penance.
signature_moments.source_phrase: that will was opposed by longing to do penance
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It reverses the simple external-punishment model and sets up Jiang's free-will reading.

chronology_notes.note: This packet captures the hinge where Jiang's June 26 lecture turns Statius's lines on free will into a sustained investigation of chosen penance.

uncertainty_notes.note: Anna's paraphrase is incomplete and Jiang immediately rejects it, so it should not be treated as a stable interpretive claim.
